title: Live networks and firewalls
description: Inspect the deployed resources and apply explicit runtime changes. Operations are recorded in deployment history.
invalidState: The backend returned an invalid runtime state.
failed: The runtime operation could not start.
unavailable: Install a matching backend and SDN runtime to enable these operations.
queued: Operation {id} started. Follow its progress in the attempt history and logs.
prerequisites: Filtering requires the datacenter switch, VM switch and each NIC flag. Inspect every level before relying on enforcement.
forwardingUnknown: Forwarding has not been tested from the guest.
natScope: This applies SDN changes and reconciles live SNAT rules across the shared host. Other subnets retain their declared settings. The saved Git scenario stays visible as the original intent.
nativeNatScope: This applies SDN changes on the shared host. The selected subnet changes; other subnets retain their prior live SNAT state. Rule readback does not prove guest forwarding. The saved Git scenario retains the original intent.
firewallScope: The backend verifies VM ownership, applies the bundled management-access and NIC sequence, and reads the resulting state. Missing scenario guests are reported in the result.
sharedAck: I have reviewed the shared-host effect of this SDN operation.
desiredUnconfirmed: Requested state was not fully confirmed

git.title: Runtime changes in Git
git.description: New changes and their results are saved on the connected project’s working branch. Use the project’s repository actions to publish them.
git.policyHint: These records retain the request and outcome. Configure the scenario to apply a policy on future deployments.
git.missingProject: Open the project registered for this deployment and connect its repository to save these changes to Git.
git.cacheError: Saved in Git, but the browser copy could not be updated: {message}
git.localConflict: This runtime record was edited locally. Review the file before saving the recorded operation.

observeScope: This read-only attempt checks the selected node and records native NAT rules for the declared networks. It does not test guest traffic.
hostAck: I authorize the cluster-wide switch and the selected node’s management-access changes.
hostScope: The datacenter switch affects filtering across the cluster, including unrelated guests. Enabling first guarantees unrestricted inbound management access on TCP 22 and 8006 at datacenter and selected-node scope using the native guards. Disabling retains those rules. The saved scenario is unchanged.

report.title: Rules and observations
report.partial: Some scopes could not be read. Missing observations remain unknown.
report.traffic: Traffic has not been tested. Switch configuration and rule observations are separate evidence.
report.emptyRules: No configured rules in this chain.
report.natUnknown: Live rules are unknown. Run a native observation to read the selected node.
report.historical: Recorded observation; state may have changed since this attempt.
report.noNat: No source-scoped NAT rules were observed for these declared networks.

reasons.all_switches_enabled_traffic_unverified: All required switches are enabled; traffic remains unverified.

network.preparation: Create each new network here before starting the guests if you want to delete it here afterward. Existing shared networks stay in place.
network.scope: Only this VNet and its subnet are changed. Deletion requires verified ownership and no attached guests or templates; the shared zone is preserved. Applying SDN affects the cluster. Other networks retain their prior NAT rule counts. The saved scenario stays unchanged and may recreate the network on a later deployment.

policy.ruleChanged: This rule changed or moved since you selected it. Your draft is kept here. Select Edit on the current rule to load its latest settings before reviewing a change.
policy.aliasChanged: This alias changed or was removed since you selected it. Your draft is kept here. Select Rename on the current alias to load its latest settings before reviewing a change.
policy.title: Firewall policies and aliases
policy.scopeHint: These runtime changes affect the selected scope. Datacenter policies can affect other nodes and guests. Management rules are protected; referenced aliases cannot be renamed or deleted. New rules are inserted first. The saved scenario remains unchanged and a later deployment may restore its declared settings.
policy.newRule: Add rule at the start of the chain
policy.name: Name
policy.ack: I have reviewed the scope, rule order and affected resources.
